overview: The Community Preservation Committee heard presentations on the first batch of five applications for the current funding round, spanning open space improvements, historic church restoration, and municipal facility renovations. The committee also approved its September 10 minutes and reviewed available funding balances.

items.title: Riverside Plaza Shade Structure
items.summary: Amanda Centrella presented an application for approximately $144,000 in CPA matching funds to install shade sails, a permeable deck, and a water filling station at Riverside Plaza.

items.title: Carr Park Renovation Phase 2
items.summary: Amanda Centrella requested roughly $150,000 in CPA funding for construction administration and final phase components of the Carr Park project.

items.title: Unitarian Universalist Church Exterior Restoration
items.summary: Liz Ammons requested $90,000 to restore wood trim and reshingle the north and west exterior walls of the historic 1894 church building.

items.title: City Hall Restroom ADA Upgrades
items.summary: Paul Righi and Frances Nwajei presented a $250,000 application to fund an architectural study and initial construction to bring City Hall restrooms into ADA compliance while preserving original marble surfaces where feasible.

items.title: Hegner Center Building Restoration
items.summary: Paul Righi presented a proposal for exterior window, door, and roof repairs to support converting the Hegner Center into a community resiliency center and recreation programming space.

items.title: Meeting Minutes: September 10, 2024
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of the September 10, 2024 meeting.

items.title: Funding Round Financial Review
items.summary: The committee reviewed total funding requests across all submitted applications relative to available budgeted and undesignated CPA funds ahead of upcoming deliberations.
